author: Atlas
bindings: Each PC keeps its own authoritative production watchlist, authenticated read-only market-data connection, model recipes and manual trader controls. The Atlas watchlist/profile binding matches eleven members; no private credential value or account state is included.
limitations: Offline provider-mocked verification; existing local provider bindings were inspected without a live request, so current server authentication and availability are unverified.
Combined Tk suites showed transient interpreter setup failures/skips; preserved original outcomes and independently reran every skipped applicable case passing.
Scout source and the stacked Atlas test PR remain separate from common-main integration.
loaded_runtime: The synthetic product preview loaded the installed source; the normal desktop application has not been observed loading it and awaits its next normal launch.
ownership: Scout retains the shared calculation/widget implementation; Atlas adopts it fieldwise into its existing Stats composition and owns local verification and installation.
price_policy: One UTC T per refresh; latest completed positive-volume native Schwab extended-hours minute closes at or before T and T minus 24 elapsed hours, with fresh FMP split comparability. XNAS closures retain actual timestamps; more than ten missing regular-session minutes is stale. Full equal-weight average requires all local members and uses unrounded changes.
runtime_implications: The panel refreshes independently of saved prediction/order readers and filters. Normal desktop loading, local source installation and source publication are distinct. No trader process, trading control or schedule was operated for verification.
summary: Atlas adopts the shared rolling 24-hour price panel and publishes portable local-profile layout checks
